Original real signed macOS XPC/CDHash six remain mandatory serial unchanged; local adhoc signer not production operator

R4 uses held allowed-signers FD through OpenSSH; R5 examines same-inode write-restore and A-B-A pathname reversion under true second-process OS edits

Twelve native admission gates not satisfied by local FD, ctime, hashes or signed self-assertions

findings.finding: An open descriptor preserves inode, not immutable bytes. Same-admin second process can write alternate bytes in place and restore the originals
findings.test: Actual child process in-place write+fsync+restore+mtime reset, R4 check must refuse through observed ctime change

findings.finding: Two coordinated public-key and allowed-signers files can be modified then restored, yielding matching final bytes without independent history
findings.test: Actual subprocess paired in-place writes and restores while old R4 guard holds both original FDs

findings.finding: A pathname can transiently name a distinct inode and later return to its original inode; equality of final inode or content hashes alone does not rule out intervening change
findings.test: Actual second-process rename A -> hold, B -> A, B back, A restored; inspect actual kernel st_ctime_ns and R4 refusal

findings.finding: After coherent rollback of three genuine local files, fresh OS process observes old state without external evidence that newer state was once committed
findings.test: Replay prior actual R5Q three-file history and fresh-process witnessed missing monotonic floor; never grant native authority

findings.finding: Kernel-managed ctime detection in an uninterrupted process is not an externally immutable high-water history, and full same-admin memory/kernel control remains outside scoped protection
findings.test: Retain all twelve native gates blocked and zero falsely claimed independent specialists
